note: Syngeneic mouse tumours with a surrogate anti-CTLA-4 predicted the class; in NSCLC the ipilimumab-chemotherapy regimen failed its Phase 3 after a positive Phase 2, while the mouse-predicted anti-PD-1 combination (CheckMate 227, 9LA) succeeded; safety transfers from melanoma, where monkeys missed and knockout mice called the autoimmune harm.
label: NSCLC (anti-CTLA-4)

engagement.confidence_note: Model class filed with melanoma BLA 125377 (SA1/N, MC38, CT26 in hCTLA-4 transgenic mice; 9D9 surrogate); the 2020 NSCLC supplements were not read.

engagement.note: The founding model read out tumour rejection and re-challenge immunity, not a pharmacodynamic marker; no NSCLC patient readout has been compared with it.
engagement.short: Mouse readout was rejection, not PD
engagement.quote: Furthermore, this rejection resulted in immunity to a secondary exposure to tumor cells.

engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading. The BLA review also documents a 2009 Medarex MC38 anti-PD-1 plus anti-CTLA-4 study (report 930036349).
engagement.judgement: Perets 2021 (quavonlimab plus pembrolizumab, NSCLC) found circulating CD4+ counts correlated with response, a peripheral downstream readout, not the model's intratumoural one, so it is not scored. Melanoma engagement data (ICOS+ T cells) are not imported: imported_from is a safety field.
engagement.model: B16, MC38 and CT26 tumours in mice with anti-mouse CTLA-4 plus anti-PD-1
engagement.note: Combination model read intratumoural effector:regulatory T-cell ratios; NSCLC trials of nivolumab-ipilimumab reported no tumour T-cell readout to set beside it.
engagement.short: Teff:Treg readout never measured in NSCLC
engagement.quote: Combination PD-1 and CTLA-4 blockade increases effector T-cell (Teff) infiltration, resulting in highly advantageous Teff-to-regulatory T-cell ratios with the tumor.

dose.confidence_note: Model class filed with melanoma BLA 125377 (SA1/N, MC38, CT26 in hCTLA-4 transgenic mice; 9D9 surrogate); the 2020 NSCLC supplements were not read.

dose.note: Mouse antibody doses were set empirically; no exposure or occupancy target was stated, so nothing carried into patients.
dose.quote: Here, in vivo administration of antibodies to CTLA-4 resulted in the rejection of tumors, including preestablished tumors.

dose.model: B16, MC38 and CT26 tumours in mice with anti-mouse CTLA-4 plus anti-PD-1

dose.quote: Adding alphaPD-L1 to this regimen results in rejection of 65% of preimplanted tumors vs. 10% with CTLA-4 blockade alone.

dose.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading; the 10 mg/kg dose is from the Phase 3 abstract and trial design, not stated in this abstract. The surrogate antibody, not ipilimumab, was in the mouse.
dose.judgement: Scored by the efficacy-tied rule (reached, worked). The mouse gave no transferable exposure target; the human dose came from melanoma. Partial because only the phased schedule met the gate.
dose.model: Syngeneic mouse tumours (colon carcinoma, fibrosarcoma) with hamster anti-mouse CTLA-4
dose.note: Ipilimumab 10 mg/kg, the melanoma-tested dose, with carboplatin-paclitaxel; the phased schedule met its irPFS gate, so the dose was reached and sufficient.
dose.quote: The study met its primary end point of improved irPFS for phased ipilimumab versus the control (hazard ratio [HR], 0.72; P = .05), but not for concurrent ipilimumab (HR, 0.81; P = .13).

dose.judgement: Year 2016 because registry results (NCT01285609) posted 2016-06-23, before the 2017 JCO paper. Dose failure is derived from the efficacy failure and counted once; no toxicity block, since the dose was given as planned.
dose.model: Syngeneic mouse tumours (colon carcinoma, fibrosarcoma) with hamster anti-mouse CTLA-4
dose.note: Phase 3 gave the same 10 mg/kg phased regimen to 749 squamous NSCLC patients; OS HR 0.91, regimen abandoned: the reached dose was not enough.
dose.quote: randomly assigned (1:1) to receive paclitaxel and carboplatin plus blinded ipilimumab 10 mg/kg or placebo every 3 weeks on a phased induction schedule comprising six chemotherapy cycles

dose.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading; the 1 mg/kg q6w regimen is from the CheckMate 9LA abstract and the trial design, not stated in this abstract.
dose.judgement: Scored by the efficacy-tied rule. Selby 2016 (10.1371/journal.pone.0161779) showed in MC38 that activity held with a fixed anti-CTLA-4 dose and falling anti-PD-1 doses, the reverse of the human de-escalation of ipilimumab, so no mouse margin is claimed (margin_stated null).
dose.model: B16, MC38 and CT26 tumours in mice with anti-mouse CTLA-4 plus anti-PD-1
dose.note: Ipilimumab 1 mg/kg every 6 weeks with nivolumab, a dose set by CheckMate 012 tolerability rather than the mouse; OS met, so reached and sufficient.
dose.quote: the median duration of overall survival was 17.1 months (95% confidence interval [CI], 15.0 to 20.1) with nivolumab plus ipilimumab and 14.9 months (95% CI, 12.7 to 16.7) with chemotherapy (P = 0.007)

efficacy.confidence_note: Model class filed with melanoma BLA 125377 (SA1/N, MC38, CT26 in hCTLA-4 transgenic mice; 9D9 surrogate); the 2020 NSCLC supplements were not read.
efficacy.model: Syngeneic mouse tumours (colon carcinoma, fibrosarcoma) with hamster anti-mouse CTLA-4
efficacy.note: Anti-CTLA-4 rejected transplanted colon carcinoma and fibrosarcoma but not poorly immunogenic B16; no lung tumour was tested and no patient comparison existed.
efficacy.short: Mouse rejects transplanted tumours; no lung model
efficacy.quote: Here, in vivo administration of antibodies to CTLA-4 resulted in the rejection of tumors, including preestablished tumors.

efficacy.model: B16, MC38 and CT26 tumours in mice with anti-mouse CTLA-4 plus anti-PD-1
efficacy.note: Dual blockade more than doubled B16 rejection with vaccine; the Medarex MC38 study filed with the BLA showed the same; no patient test yet.
efficacy.short: Dual blockade doubles rejection in mice
efficacy.quote: Here, we show that the combination of CTLA-4 and PD-1 blockade is more than twice as effective as either alone in promoting the rejection of B16 melanomas in conjunction with Fvax.

efficacy.magnitude_basis: tumour rejection in mice vs irPFS hazard ratio 0.72
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading; irPFS is an immune-related surrogate, P = .05.
efficacy.judgement: The model side is the generic rejection model (Leach 1996), since ipilimumab monotherapy was never tested against a primary endpoint in NSCLC; the chemotherapy pairing was the first NSCLC test of the class. Partial: one of two ipilimumab schedules met the gate.
efficacy.model: Syngeneic mouse tumours (colon carcinoma, fibrosarcoma) with hamster anti-mouse CTLA-4
efficacy.note: Randomised Phase 2 (n=204): phased ipilimumab with carboplatin-paclitaxel met its irPFS primary endpoint (HR 0.72); the concurrent schedule did not.
efficacy.short: Phase 2 irPFS met, phased schedule only
efficacy.quote: The study met its primary end point of improved irPFS for phased ipilimumab versus the control (hazard ratio [HR], 0.72; P = .05), but not for concurrent ipilimumab (HR, 0.81; P = .13).

patient_trials.quote: Phased ipilimumab plus paclitaxel and carboplatin improved irPFS and PFS, which supports additional investigation of ipilimumab in NSCLC.

efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading of a Phase 3 with an OS primary endpoint.
efficacy.judgement: Year 2016 from the registry results posting (2016-06-23), before the 2017 paper. Contra rather than neg: the mouse never tested a lung tumour, so it held no below-bar datum for this regimen; Leach's B16 non-response is a different tumour. A failed track stays failed, so the later nivolumab-ipilimumab success is booked on its own dual-blockade track.
efficacy.model: Syngeneic mouse tumours (colon carcinoma, fibrosarcoma) with hamster anti-mouse CTLA-4
efficacy.note: Phase 3 in squamous NSCLC: OS 13.4 vs 12.4 months, HR 0.91, P=0.25; ipilimumab plus chemotherapy was abandoned in NSCLC.
efficacy.quote: Median OS was 13.4 months for chemotherapy plus ipilimumab and 12.4 months for chemotherapy plus placebo (hazard ratio, 0.91; 95% CI, 0.77 to 1.07; P = .25).

patient_trials.quote: Median progression-free survival was 5.6 months for both groups (hazard ratio, 0.87; 95% CI, 0.75 to 1.01).

efficacy.magnitude_basis: rejection fraction in mice vs OS medians 17.1 vs 14.9 months
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading; registry results were first posted 2025-10-30, after the paper.
efficacy.judgement: Separate track from the chemotherapy-combination failure: the dual-blockade mice (Curran 2010; Medarex MC38 2009; Selby 2016) are a different prediction system, and the brief makes a newer model that did better its own track. If the atlas prefers one track per mouse system, this entry cannot flip the 2016 contra and the cell stays contra. Selby 2016 states its models predicted the melanoma combination result, not NSCLC, so comparison_stated is false here.
efficacy.model: B16, MC38 and CT26 tumours in mice with anti-mouse CTLA-4 plus anti-PD-1
efficacy.note: CheckMate 227: nivolumab plus ipilimumab beat chemotherapy on OS in PD-L1 >=1% NSCLC (17.1 vs 14.9 months, P=0.007); the combination the mice predicted worked.
efficacy.quote: the median duration of overall survival was 17.1 months (95% confidence interval [CI], 15.0 to 20.1) with nivolumab plus ipilimumab and 14.9 months (95% CI, 12.7 to 16.7) with chemotherapy (P = 0.007)

patient_trials.quote: The median duration of response was 23.2 months with nivolumab plus ipilimumab and 6.2 months with chemotherapy.

efficacy.magnitude_basis: rejection fraction in mice vs OS hazard ratio 0.69
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading; year 2020 from the registry results posting (2020-09-16) and the 2020-05-26 FDA approval, before the 2021 paper.
efficacy.judgement: Strengthens, not a new status. Pfirschke 2016 (10.1016/j.immuni.2015.11.024) showed in Kras/Trp53 lung adenocarcinoma mice that immunogenic chemotherapy sensitises to anti-PD-1 plus anti-CTLA-4, but with oxaliplatin-cyclophosphamide, not a platinum doublet, and nobody compared it with 9LA, so it is not a track. Quavonlimab (Perets 2021, NCT03179436) is single-arm with a safety primary endpoint and changes no status; zalifrelimab has no NSCLC result in PubMed. Tremelimumab (POSEIDON) is not a member and is not scored.
efficacy.model: B16, MC38 and CT26 tumours in mice with anti-mouse CTLA-4 plus anti-PD-1
efficacy.note: CheckMate 9LA: nivolumab-ipilimumab plus two chemotherapy cycles beat chemotherapy on OS in all-comers (14.1 vs 10.7 months, HR 0.69); FDA approved May 2020.
efficacy.quote: overall survival in all randomly assigned patients was significantly longer in the experimental group than in the control group (median 14·1 months [95% CI 13·2-16·2] vs 10·7 months [9·5-12·4]; hazard ratio [HR] 0·69 [96·71% CI 0·55-0·87]; p=0·00065)

patient_trials.quote: Nivolumab plus ipilimumab with two cycles of chemotherapy provided a significant improvement in overall
Efficacy was observed at all dose levels/schedules in patients with NSCLC.

efficacy.reason: Dual-blockade mice right; chemo-combo mice wrong

safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading; the FDA review (section 9.2) reviews Tivol and Waterhouse 1995 in full.
safety.note: CTLA-4-deficient mice die of multi-organ lymphoproliferation by 3-4 weeks: a standing prediction of autoimmune harm before any patient was dosed.
safety.quote: These mice rapidly develop lymphoproliferative disease with multiorgan lymphocytic infiltration and tissue destruction, with particularly severe myocarditis and pancreatitis, and die by 3-4 weeks of age.

safety.confidence_note: First monkey use inferred from the 2000 cross-reactivity study (IM578) listed in the review; the first repeat-dose study date was not extracted. Review read in passages, not in full.
safety.note: The monkey was the only pharmacologically responsive species (ipilimumab binds no rodent CTLA-4) and carried all GLP toxicology.
safety.short: Monkey the only responsive tox species
safety.quote: Initial nonclinical studies conducted by the sponsor identified the non-human primate as the only pharmacologically responsive test animal species

safety.magnitude_basis: organ pattern: myocarditis and pancreatitis in mice vs enterocolitis, hepatitis and endocrinopathy in patients
safety.confidence_note: Patient side is the FDA review's summary of the melanoma Phase 2/3 trials; NSCLC trials were not re-read for irAE rates beyond their abstracts.
safety.judgement: Ipilimumab does not bind mouse CTLA-4, so the knockout stands in for complete blockade. The review's own knockout discussion concerns prenatal exposure; the pairing with adult irAEs is mine (comparison_stated false). Myocarditis, the knockout's dominant lesion, is rare in patients, so the match is directional. Comparison made in melanoma and imported; NSCLC trials show the same profile (Lynch 2012: grade 3-4 irAEs 15-20%; 9LA: diarrhoea, hepatitis and pneumonitis deaths).
safety.note: Patients on 3-10 mg/kg had severe and fatal autoimmune enterocolitis, hepatitis, dermatitis, neuropathy and endocrinopathies: the knockout's multi-organ autoimmunity, in direction.
safety.quote: severe and fatal autoimmune-mediated enterocolitis, hepatitis, dermatitis (including toxic epidermal necrolysis), neuropathy, and endocrinopathies

safety.confidence_note: Verbatim from the review's executive summary; quote is a sentence fragment to fit 40 words.
safety.judgement: FDA attributes the miss to 3-fold weaker monkey binding and shorter dosing. Selby 2016 later reported dose-dependent GI inflammation in monkeys given ipilimumab plus nivolumab, absent in single-agent studies; it followed the 2013 melanoma combination data and a contra track stays contra. Imported from melanoma; the 9LA NSCLC treatment-related deaths (diarrhoea, hepatitis, pneumonitis) are the same harms.
safety.note: FDA: monkey toxicity was minimal (lymphocyte infiltrates, lymph-node hyperplasia) and did not reflect the severe, fatal autoimmune enterocolitis, hepatitis and endocrinopathies in trials.
safety.quote: the toxicities observed in the single- and repeat-dose toxicity studies of ipilimumab in cynomolgus monkeys did not reflect the clinical toxicities observed in the phase 2 and phase 3 trials, namely, severe and fatal autoimmune-mediated enterocolitis, hepatitis, dermatitis

safety.magnitude_basis: colitis onset and severity in mice vs patient enterocolitis
safety.confidence_note: Study 930031040, report dated 2008-10-15, used BMS-863019 (a hamster anti-mouse CTLA-4), not ipilimumab.
safety.judgement: Retrodiction: the model was built after the clinic knew the answer (melanoma enterocolitis reported from 2003), so retro, never same. It did not require a disease model to exist; the reviewer's statement of comparability is the stated comparison.
safety.model: Oxazolone and TNBS mouse colitis with hamster anti-mouse CTLA-4
safety.note: Run in 2008 after enterocolitis was known from melanoma trials: surrogate anti-CTLA-4 worsened two colitis models, which FDA called comparable to patients' GI toxicity.
safety.quote: In two models of auto-immune related colitis, the surrogate anti-CTLA-4 antibody “exacerbated the onset and severity of the disease” (report p 7). The treatment-related toxicity was comparable to the gastrointestinal toxicity observed in patients receiving ipilimumab.
safety.reason: Knockout right, monkeys wrong, colitis retrodicted

safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading (PMID 16037385). Not cited in the BLA 125377 pharmacology review text.
safety.note: Human CTLA4 knock-in mice built after melanoma irAEs were reported; anti-human CTLA-4 antibodies gave tumour rejection with mild autoimmunity, never set beside patient data.
safety.quote: we have generated human CTLA4 gene knock-in mice and used them to compare a panel of anti-human CTLA-4 antibodies for their ability to induce tumor rejection and autoimmunity.
safety.judgement: Opening entry at first use of the system. The paper was motivated by the melanoma irAE reports but states no side-by-side comparison; Du 2018 later says this adult-mouse version 'failed to recapitulate clinical observations' because its autoimmunity was mild, a judgement not available in 2005 (rule 7).
safety.model: Human CTLA4 knock-in (Ctla4h/h) mice dosed with ipilimumab, alone or with anti-PD-1

safety.magnitude_basis: organ pattern: mouse myocarditis, anaemia/red-cell aplasia and heart, lung, liver, kidney, gut inflammation vs patient grade 3-4 irAEs (colitis, hepatitis, pneumonitis, dermatitis); no incidence or exposure comparison
safety.confidence_note: Full text read (PMC5939041). Severe irAEs required dosing perinatal mice (from birth, read at 6 weeks); 6-7-week-old adults showed milder heart and kidney lesions. Patient side is the paper's own citation of CheckMate 012 (NSCLC) and CheckMate 067 (melanoma); the NSCLC supplements to BLA 125377 were not read.
safety.note: Ipilimumab, alone and with anti-PD-1, gave perinatal knock-in mice severe multi-organ irAEs and red-cell aplasia, reproducing the irAE profile known from NSCLC and melanoma trials.
safety.short: Ipilimumab irAEs reproduced in humanised mice
safety.quote: In this model, the clinically used drug, Ipilimumab, induced severe irAE especially when combined with an anti-PD-1 antibody; whereas another mAb, L3D10, induced comparable CITE with very mild irAE under the same conditions.
safety.judgement: Retrodiction, so retro, never same: the model was tuned (perinatal dosing, anti-PD-1 combination) to reproduce irAEs known from melanoma since 2003 and from NSCLC combination cohorts (Hellmann 2017 CheckMate 012, 10.1016/S1470-2045(16)30624-6), both of which the paper cites as the patient side, so comparison_stated true and no import. Separate track from ctla4-knockout-mouse (loss of function, no antibody) and from the BLA hCTLA-4 transgenic tumour mice (efficacy prediction): different model and a different, product-level safety prediction. Match is in direction only; myocarditis and anaemia dominate the mouse, colitis and hepatitis the patients. Its forward prediction (L3D10/HL12 safer) has no patient test.
safety.model: Human CTLA4 knock-in (Ctla4h/h) mice dosed with ipilimumab, alone or with anti-PD-1

safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading (PMID 33257470); full text not retrievable from Europe PMC within budget. Epub 2020-11-30, print March 2021.
safety.note: Compound mutant mice (one Ctla4 allele lost on a Pdcd1-null background) built to model myocarditis under combined CTLA-4 and PD-1 loss; no antibody is dosed.
safety.quote: Here, we report a robust preclinical mouse model of ICI-associated myocarditis in which monoallelic loss of Ctla4 in the context of complete genetic absence of Pdcd1 leads to premature death in approximately half of mice.
safety.judgement: Opening entry at first use, same year as its comparison. A different system from ctla4-knockout-mouse: heterozygous Ctla4 on a Pdcd1-null background, modelling the combination regimen's cardiac harm rather than complete CTLA-4 loss.
safety.model: Ctla4+/- Pdcd1-/- compound mutant mice (genetic ICI-myocarditis model)

safety.magnitude_basis: myocardial T-cell and macrophage infiltration with ECG abnormalities, as in patient ICI myocarditis; the model's ~50% penetrance is a genetic dose, not a drug incidence
safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading; the paper's patient side is ICI-myocarditis cases across cancers (its own abatacept case series and the literature), not an NSCLC cohort, hence imported from cancer (MONDO:0004992). Clinical myocarditis incidence is about 1%, so the match is qualitative.
safety.note: Mice lacking Pdcd1 and one Ctla4 allele died of T-cell and macrophage myocarditis with ECG changes, reproducing myocarditis reported on ipilimumab plus nivolumab since 2016.
safety.quote: Premature death results from myocardial infiltration by T cells and macrophages and severe ECG abnormalities, closely recapitulating the clinical and pathologic hallmarks of ICI-associated myocarditis observed in patients.
safety.judgement: Retrodiction: built after fulminant myocarditis on ipilimumab plus nivolumab was reported (Johnson 2016 NEJM, melanoma), so retro, never same; the source states the comparison. Models the class's combination harm (ipilimumab plus anti-PD-1, the NSCLC regimen of CheckMate 227 and 9LA) without dosing any antibody, so product_in_model false. Direction only: the human comparison is organ and histology pattern, not incidence. Its forward prediction (abatacept rescue) was tested only in a case series, not scored.
safety.model: Ctla4+/- Pdcd1-/- compound mutant mice (genetic ICI-myocarditis model)
